newsitem.title: USA: China's military chief meets Cohen, Albright.
newsitem.headline: China's military chief meets Cohen, Albright.

text.p: China's military chief met with U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on Friday in a visit to improve relations frozen after Chinese soldiers crushed demonstrations in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in 1989.

Gen. Fu Quanyou, chief of staff of the People's Liberation Army, was greeted in a full honours ceremony at the Pentagon, complete with 19-gun salute, by his American counterpart, Gen. John Shalikashvili, chairman of the military Joint Chiefs of Staff.
Fu also met later with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, a U.S. official said.

In discussions at the Pentagon, Fu and U.S. officials agreed that four-party talks on Korea should continue, according to a Defence Department official. The talks in New York this week between U.S., Chinese, North Korean and South Korean diplomats broke off on Thursday.

Shalikashvili expressed pleasure that Fu had been able to keep an earlier promise to help U.S. military ships keep their established schedule of port calls to Hong Kong following the handover to China last month, the defence official said.
The question of Taiwan, often a bone of contention in U.S.-China relations, did not come up in Pentagon discussions, according to the defence official.
This was a reciprocal visit for Fu, who hosted Shalikashvili in Beijing in May.

At those earlier meetings, Shalikashvili said he favoured better military ties with China, but voiced concern about regional stability, and applauded moves toward "rational dialogue" over the question of Taiwan.

Noting the Clinton administration's desire for a politically stable and economically open China with respect for human rights and the rule of law, Shalikashvili said in May that military-to-military contacts would foster better understanding and cooperation between the two countries.
Aside from Washington, Fu has made stops at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, New York, the U.S. Army's Fort Bragg, North Carolina, and Langley Air Force Base in Virginia.
He was scheduled to leave Washington on Saturday for a visit to San Francisco and to the U.S. Pacific Command in Hawaii before returning to China on Aug. 13.

A number of Western countries have recently moved to improve military ties with China, following an effective freeze in relations after Chinese soldiers put down student-led pro-democracy protests in Beijing in 1989 with heavy loss of life.
